question: The European Defence Fund (EDF) Regulation1 says that in case of transfer of ownership of results generated by recipients through development actions supported by the fund to a nonassociated non-EU country or to a non-associated non-EU country entity, the Commission shall be notified prior to any such transfer. When this transfer contravenes the security and defence interests of the EU and its Member States or the objectives of the fund, the support provided shall be reimbursed2. 1.
Does the Commission have a mechanism in place to check that no transfers are made without prior notification of the Commission?

The Commission claims to have a mechanism in place to assess whether a transfer of ownership to a non-associated non-EU country or non-associated non-EU country entity contravenes the security and defence interests of the EU and its Member States, or the objectives set out in Article 3 of the EDF Regulation. What criteria does this mechanism use?

As the Commission refuses to publicise not just the content, but even the mere existence of notifications under Article 23(4), can the Commission clarify what mechanisms allow democratic oversight, scrutiny and accountability in this regard?
OJ L 170, 12.5.2021, p. 149, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2021/697/oj. https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/E-10-2025-003832-ASW_EN.html.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (4.3.2026) The grant agreement signed with the consortium requires beneficiaries to notify the Commission in advance of any transfer of ownership or licensing of results to a nonassociated third country or entity. Compliance with this contractual obligation may be verified ex post by the Commission, in particular through audits.

The assessment involves checking whether the third country is subject to any restrictive measures adopted by the Council in the framework of the Common Foreign and Security Policy (e.g. arms embargos, restriction on admissions, asset freezes and other economic measures such as restrictions on imports and exports).

The assessment would also check whether the transfer could contravene the objectives in Article 3 of the European Defence Fund (EDF) Regulation1. Notifications made under Article 23(4) of the EDF Regulation are not intended to be made public.
The assessment as to whether access is possible may take place following the submission of a request for access to documents, which is assessed in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 1049/20012.
